verses.zh: 论摩押的默示：一夜之间，摩押的亚珥变为荒废，归于无有；一夜之间，摩押的基珥变为荒废，归于无有。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about Moab:Indeed, in a night it is devastated,Ar of Moab is destroyed!Indeed, in a night it is devastated,Kir of Moab is destroyed!
verses.commentary:
15:1 Notice how Isaiah's contextual marker of a new message or vision "oracle" (BDB 672 III) appears in
Isa. 15:1. See note at Isa. 13:1 (cf. Isa. 14:28; 17:1; 19:1; 21:1,11,13; 22:1; 23:1; 30:6). This term denotes
a divine revelation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣ "Moab" This is one of Israel's relatives from Lot and one of his two daughters after their
flight from Sodom (cf. Genesis 19). Moab, Ammon, and Edom (i.e. the trans-Jordan nations) are first
mentioned as receiving domination by Judah in Isa. 11:14.

Chapters 15-16 form a literary unit dealing with Moab's judgment (cf. Jeremiah 48; Ezek. 25:8-11;
Amos 2:1-3; Zeph. 2:8-11). Moab is mentioned often in the book of Numbers because Israel had to travel through their
land to get to Canaan. Moses was buried there (cf. Deuteronomy 34).

▣ "Surely in a night" This phrase is repeated twice and emphasizes the suddenness and completeness
of the coming judgment of Moabite cities.

The two VERBS "devastated" (BDB 994, KB 1418) and "ruined"
(lit. "cut off," BDB 198, KB 225) are both PERFECTS (there is a series of four
PERFECT VERBS in v. 1), also denoting a complete destruction. Isaiah used the
VERB "ruined" to describe himself in Isa. 6:5.

The Assyrian armies invaded Canaan/Palestine several times.

- Sargon II in 715 B.C.

- Sargon II in 711 B.C.

- Sennacherib in 701 B.C.

▣ "Ar" The term (BDB 786 I) can refer to a city (it is the general name for city in the Moabite
language) or a region (i.e. Deut. 2:9,29).

Since Kir (BDB 885 II) also means "wall" (cf. LXX, i.e. walled city) in Hebrew, it is possible
that Ar and Kir refer to the capital of Moab in parallel poetic lines.

verses.zh: 他们上巴益，又往底本，到高处去哭泣。摩押人因尼波和米底巴哀号，各人头上光秃，胡须剃净。
verses.en: They went up to the temple;[NOTE:1] the people of Dibon went up to the high places to lament.[NOTE:2] Because of what happened to Nebo and Medeba,[NOTE:3] Moab wails.Every head is shaved bare,every beard is trimmed off.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “even Dibon [to] the high places to weep.” The verb “went up” does double duty in the parallel structure.
Shaving the head and beard were outward signs of mourning and grief.
verses.commentary:
15:2 "to the temple. . .even to the high places" This is a reference to Moabite places of worship of
Chemosh (cf. Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:46). The temple of this Canaanite deity was possibly located near Dibon,
Moab's capital. The worship of this god involved human sacrifice. Verse 9a (DSS has "Dybon," but the MT has
"Dimon") mentions "blood," which may refer to

- human sacrifice

- military invasion

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHEMOSH

▣ "Dibon. . .Nebo. . .Medeba" There are also cities of Moab listed in the book of Numbers in relation to the
Wilderness Wandering Period as Israel finally approached Canaan from the eastern side of the Jordan Rift Valley.

15:2-3 wails. . .bald. . .beard cut off. . .mourning. . .girded with sackcloth. . .wailing" These all
refer to mourning rites of the ANE (cf. Isa. 22:12; Ezra 9:3; Job 1:20; Jer. 7:29; 16:6; 41:5; 47:5; 48:37;
Ezek. 7:18; 27:31; Micah 1:16). The population tries to turn to their gods (cf. Isa. 15:2); they try to
repent and seek help, but there is no help from lifeless idols!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

verses.zh: 他们在街市上都腰束麻布，在房顶上和宽阔处俱各哀号，眼泪汪汪。
verses.en: In their streets they wear sackcloth;on their roofs and in their town squaresall of them wail;they fall down weeping.

verses.zh: 希实本和以利亚利悲哀的声音达到雅杂，所以摩押带兵器的高声喊嚷，人心战兢。
verses.en: The people of[NOTE:1] Heshbon and Elealeh cry out;their voices are heard as far away as Jahaz.For this reason Moab’s soldiers shout in distress;their courage wavers.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

The Hebrew text has, “For this reason the soldiers of Moab shout; his inner being quivers for him.” To achieve tighter parallelism, some emend the first line, changing חֲלֻצֵי (khalutse, “soldiers”) to חַלְצֵי (khaltse, “loins”) and יָרִיעוּ (yariʿu, “they shout,” from רוּעַ, ruaʿ) to יָרְעוּ (yorʿu, “they quiver”), a verb from יָרַע (yaraʿ), which also appears in the next line. One can then translate v. 4b as “For this reason the insides of the Moabites quiver; their whole body shakes” (cf. NAB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
15:4 "Heshbon. . .Elealeh. . .Jahaz" These are also cities on the eastern side of Jordan, close to and
often identified with Moab (or Ammon, i.e. Mesha Stone, 9th century B.C.).

▣ "cry out" This is the VERB (BDB 277, KB 277, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) that was used in its Qal IMPERATIVE
form in Isa. 14:31 (Philistia). Here it denotes Moab and in Isa. 15:5 it denotes YHWH or Isaiah. Note its
use in Jer. 48:20,31.

▣

NASB
"the armed men"

NKJV, Peshitta
"the armed soldiers"

NRSV, LXX, JB
"the lions"

NJB
"warriors"

REB
"stoutest warriors"

JPSOA
"the shock troops"

The difference between "soldiers" (BDB 323 II) and "loins" (BDB 323) in Hebrew
is vocalization, not a consonantal change.

▣ "His soul trembles within him" This VERB (BDB 438,
KB 440, Qal PERFECT) appears only here. There are several Hebrew words
translated "tremble." They denote fear and lack of action in the face of God's judgment. They
characterize "holy war." This one may have been chosen for poetic reasons to sound like
the VERB "cry out."

The term "soul" is nephesh and denotes air-breathing life on this planet. It is used
as imagery for a human person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 我心为摩押悲哀；他的贵胄（或译：逃民）逃到琐珥，到伊基拉・施利施亚。他们上鲁希坡，随走随哭；在何罗念的路上，因毁灭举起哀声。
verses.en: My heart cries out because of Moab’s plight[NOTE:1] and for the fugitives[NOTE:2] stretched out[NOTE:3] as far as Zoar and Eglath Shelishiyah.For they weep as they make their way up the ascent of Luhith;they loudly lament their demise on the road to Horonaim.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “for Moab.” For rhetorical purposes the speaker (the Lord?; see v. 9) plays the role of a mourner.
The vocalization of the Hebrew text suggests “the bars of her gates,” but the form should be repointed to yield, “her fugitives.” See HALOT 156-57 s.v. בָּרִחַ, and BDB 138 s.v. בָּרִיהַ.
The words “are stretched out” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “For the ascent of Luhith, with weeping they go up it; for [on] the road to Horonaim an outcry over shattering they raise up.”
verses.commentary:
15:5-9 The Jewish Study Bible sees these verses as referring to Moabites fleeing to Edom (p. 815). This
is possible because the exact location of these cities mentioned is uncertain, though all are east or
southeast of the Jordan River.

15:5 "My heart cries out for Moab" The "my" in context must refer to YHWH Himself (cf. Isa. 15:9). Although
it could be the prophet himself, cf. Isa. 16:9,11. YHWH hears the cries of Moab's people and is moved. They
still receive judgment, but not from a thoughtless, uncaring God! They are even offered help/refuge in
Isa. 16:1-4. What an amazing text!

The Septuagint changes the referent to "the heart of the region of Moab cries within her"
(cf. NJB).

▣

NASB, NRSV, TEV, REB, JPSOA
"Eglath-shelishiyah"

NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"like a three-year-old heifer" (from same root; KB 784)

This (BDB 722) seems to be a city (i.e. "third Eglath," cf. Jer. 48:34).

▣ "His fugitives" The MT has "her bars" (BDB 138,
בריחה from
בריה), but most translations change
the vocalization to "his fugitives" from מברה
(BDB 138).

verses.zh: 因为宁林的水成为干涸，青草枯干，嫩草灭没，青绿之物，一无所有。
verses.en: For the waters of Nimrim are gone;[NOTE:1] the grass is dried up,the vegetation has disappeared,and there are no plants.
notes: Heb “are waste places”; cf. NRSV “are a desolation.”
verses.commentary:
15:6 In the OT God controls the weather (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29). He brings abundance for covenant
obedience, but withholds agricultural production in the face of evil, wickedness, and rebellion (i.e. the two
ways, Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1). Moab faces both invasion (cf. Isa. 15:9a) and lack of food.

verses.zh: 因此，摩押人所得的财物和所积蓄的都要运过柳树河。
verses.en: For this reason what they have made and stored up,they carry over the Stream of the Poplars.
verses.commentary:
15:7 Moab was located on a major trade route from Egypt to Syria. She taxed all the caravans and
became wealthy.

verses.zh: 哀声遍闻摩押的四境；哀号的声音达到以基莲；哀号的声音达到比珥・以琳。
verses.en: Indeed, the cries of distress echo throughout Moabite territory;their wailing can be heard in Eglaim and Beer Elim.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to Eglaim [is] her wailing, and [to] Beer Elim [is] her wailing.”

verses.zh: 底们的水充满了血；我还要加增底们的灾难，叫狮子来追上摩押逃脱的民和那地上所余剩的人。
verses.en: Indeed, the waters of Dimon[NOTE:1] are full of blood!Indeed, I will heap even more trouble on Dimon.[NOTE:2] A lion will attack[NOTE:3] the Moabite fugitivesand the people left in the land.
notes: The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa reads “Dibon” instead of “Dimon” in this verse.
Heb “Indeed, I will place on Dimon added things.” Apparently the Lord is speaking.
The words “will attack” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
15:9

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB
"A lion" (אריה, BDB 71, MT)

NKJV
"Lions"

LXX
"I will remove the offspring"

Peshitta
"I will plot"

NEB
"a vision" (אראה)

DSS
"I give a drink" (ארוה)

the MT has "a lion for the remnant of the land." The UBS Text Project, p. 36, gave
this a "C" rating (considerable doubt), but suggested it was an allusion to 2 Kgs. 17:25 (i.e. "YHWH sent lions").

This could be

- literal, God uses wild animals to judge (i.e. 1 Kgs. 13:24-28; 2 Kgs. 17:25)

- a symbol of the Assyrian army (cf. Isa. 5:29; Jer. 50:17)

- figurative of invasion from Judah (cf. Isa. 11:14, the lion [ruler] of Judah).

There are two ways to view this strophe.

- The JPSOA significantly changes the translation of this verse (esp. lines 2-4) to make it
positive (cf. Isa. 15:5, "my").

"For I pour added (water) on Dimon

I drench it ‒ for Moab's refugees ‒ with soil (footnote, 'tears') for
its remnant" (DSS)

- The LXX of Isa. 15:9, lines 2-4, are also very different, but decidedly negative.

"For I will bring Arabs upon Remnon,

and I will remove the offspring of Moab and Ariel

and the remnant of Adama."

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS (locations mentioned in the literary unit of Isaiah 15-16)

Isaiah was very familiar with the geographical area of the Trans-Jordan (east of Jordan).

- Cities

- Ar, Isa. 15:1

- Kir, Isa. 15:1 (Kir-hareseth, 16:7,11)

- Dibon, Isa. 15:2,9

- Nebo, Isa. 15:2

- Medeba, Isa. 15:2

- Heshbon, Isa. 15:4; 16:9

- Elealeh, Isa. 15:4; 16:9

- Jahaz, Isa. 15:4

- Zoar, Isa. 15:5

- Eglath-shelishiyah, Isa. 15:5 (lit. "the Third Eglath," cf. Jer. 48:34)

- Luhith, Isa. 15:5

- Horonaim, Isa. 15:5

- Eglaim, Isa. 15:8

- Beer-elim, Isa. 15:8

- Dimon (DSS, "Dibon"), Isa. 15:9

- Sela, Isa. 16:1

- Kir-hareseth, Isa. 16:7,11

- Sibmah, Isa. 16:8,9

- Jazer, Isa. 16:8,9

- Admah (Isa. 15:9 REB)?

- Water Courses

- water of Nimrim, Isa. 15:6

- brook of Arabim (possibly a "wadi of poplars"), Isa. 15:7

- waters of Dimon, Isa. 15:9

- fords of Arnon, 16:2

- The listing of these numerous cities and water courses are to emphasize a total
destruction (the invader is unnamed and uncertain). There is a movement of refugees southward
or to Judah (cf. Isa. 16:1-4).

- Isaiah 15-16 forms a literary unit related to YHWH's dealing with Moab, also note Jer. 48 and Ezek. 25:9-11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOAB

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 15:1-9

1The oracle concerning Moab.

Surely in a night Ar of Moab is devastated and ruined;

Surely in a night Kir of Moab is devastated and ruined.

2They have gone up to the temple and to Dibon, even to the high places to weep.

Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba;

Everyone's head is bald and every beard is cut off.

3In their streets they have girded themselves with sackcloth;

On their housetops and in their squares

Everyone is wailing, dissolved in tears.

4Heshbon and Elealeh also cry out,

Their voice is heard all the way to Jahaz;

Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud;

His soul trembles within him.

5My heart cries out for Moab;

His fugitives are as far as Zoar and Eglath-shelishiyah,

For they go up the ascent of Luhith weeping;

Surely on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of distress over their ruin.

6For the waters of Nimrim are desolate.

Surely the grass is withered, the tender grass died out,

There is no green thing.

7Therefore the abundance which they have acquired and stored up

They carry off over the brook of Arabim.

8For the cry of distress has gone around the territory of Moab,

Its wail goes as far as Eglaim and its wailing even to Beer-elim.

9For the waters of Dimon are full of blood;

Surely I will bring added woes upon Dimon,

A lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
